instruction: Locate tomorrow's flights from Seattle-Tacoma International to Denver International.

metadata.explanation: Variation uses same Delta.com website with different airport pair (SEA to DEN) for tomorrow. Reuses existing getter 'get_active_tab_html_parse' and metric 'check_direct_json_object' which parse Delta's flight search results HTML. Airport codes SEA and DEN are standard IATA codes. Task complexity remains identical to original.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator has complete coverage: verifies start airport (SEA), end airport (DEN), and date (tomorrow)
Getter logic correctly extracts flight search data from Delta.com HTML using class-based selectors for date and airport codes
Metric comparison logic is sound: check_direct_json_object compares extracted JSON with expected values
Expected values are semantically correct: SEA and DEN are valid IATA airport codes, relativeTime calculation for 'tomorrow' is implemented correctly in get_rule_relativeTime
Data flow is correct: getter extracts {start, end, time} -> metric compares with expected {start: SEA, end: DEN, time: formatted_tomorrow_date}
The rule validator error appears to be a false positive - the actual JSON shows expected.type is correctly set to 'rule' (line 63)
